{{Quote|The MTT is tough and armored like a tank!|[[Cody/Legends|Commander Cody]], encountering MTTs on [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)">[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'']]</ref>}}
The '''Multi-Troop Transport (MTT)''' was a heavy [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] vehicle used by both the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] to transport [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] and [[Droideka/Legends|Droidekas]] prior to and during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The upgraded version was known as the '''Heavy Multi-Troop Transport.'''

==Characteristics==
[[File:MTT_ep1ig.png|thumb|left|MTT schematics]]
The Multi-Troop Transport was manufactured and designed by [[Baktoid Armor Workshop/Legends|Baktoid Armor Workshop]], as a modified cargo pod. Reminiscent of a jungle animal, its reactor and main engines were in the rear, in classic Baktoid style. The MTT could carry a company<ref name="TCWCG" /> of 112 [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]], comprising 100 infantry, 10 security droids, and 2 commanders,<ref name="Secrets of Naboo">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref> all of which were equipped with their standard [[E-5 blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifles]]. The folded droids hanged from a hydraulically powered deployment rack that extended out from the face of the MTT, allowing the droids to be deployed directly into combat if needed. The rack was also detachable.<ref name="TPMICS" />

The MTT's face was reinforced and studded with case-hardened metal alloy studs and was designed to smash through enemy walls to reach its destination. With heavy armor and weaponry, the strongest Baktoid had ever made, the MTT was almost unstoppable.<ref name="TPMICS" />

The MTT's control room was staffed by an [[OOM pilot battle droid/Legends|OOM pilot battle droid]] and a droid gunner/engineer. It was armed with only a quartet of 17kv anti-personnel [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannons]] twin-mounted in two ball turrets.<ref name="TPMICS" />

After the Battle of Naboo, it became clear that the MTT's deployed too slowly. Further models employed during the Clone Wars, including the ones used during the [[Battle of Muunilinst/Legends|Battle of Muunilinst]], deployed soldiers in standing and battle-ready position, four units at a time, allowing for immediate deployment of droids efficiently and reducing vulnerability. Some were also repainted in Separatist colors and retrofitted with new racks that could carry 12 [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|super battle droids]].<ref name="Massacre" />

The MTT was capable of being upgraded to a more powerful version, the Heavy Multi-Troop Transport.<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

Since the MTT was armed with twin blaster cannons, it was an obvious counterpart of the unarmed [[Platoon Attack Craft/Legends|Platoon Attack Craft]], which served a similar function. The MTT's weapons allowed it to deploy its [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] on the front line, whereas the PAC was used to drop off troops and leave the battle. The MTT was originally manufactured by Baktoid on the planet of [[Ord Cestus/Legends|Ord Cestus]].<ref name="The Cestus Deception">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref>

==History==
[[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Sidious]] instructed Baktoid Armor Workshop to produce an army that did not give the appearance of being an army. They designed the MTT to look like an upscaled [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Cargo pod/Legends|repulsorlift cargo pod]]. If a Trade Federation ship was inspected, their army of MTTs wouldn't be recognized as an army, but as a fleet of cargo haulers.<ref name=":0">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> 

In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], a representative from Baktoid Armor Workshop presented the first prototypes of the MTT to [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], legal counsel [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]], [[Deputy Viceroy]] [[Hath Monchar]], and [[Commander/Legends|commander]] [[Daultay Dofine/Legends|Daultay Dofine]] aboard the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk-''class battleship]] ''[[Acquisitor (Lucrehulk-class battleship)|Acquisitor]]'' in the [[Senex system/Legends|Senex system]].<ref name=":0" />  

The MTT's first deployment was during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="TPMICS" /> They were landed on the far side of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] and attacked the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]], [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] in the early morning.<ref name="SW:CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> Two MTTs transported Trade Federation troops to the [[Invasion of Spinnaker|occupation of]] [[Spinnaker/Legends|Spinnaker]].<ref name="SW:GB" />

[[File:MuunilinstMTTs-TCWCG.jpg|thumb|right|Updated model of the MTT, which deployed droids four units at a time in battle-ready position]]
MTTs also deployed legions of battle droids during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]. Following the destruction of the [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|Droid Control Ship]], all elements of the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] on Naboo shut down.<ref name="SWE1">{{Film|I}}</ref>

The original Baktoid design for the MTT called for an open staging chamber, but Baktoid's eccentric designers had the unusual job of making a transport that had to convey droids, not living beings. They thus devised a system that could load folded battle droids onto a giant deployment rack. This more than doubled the troop capacity of the MTT, which extended the droid rack to deploy the compressed troops, which would then unfold into fighting position. At the end of the battle, they'd be refolded and loaded back onto the rack to be transported back to the base. However, the open chamber was retained for storing [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]].<ref name="TPMICS" />

[[File:MTTCIS-SWE.png|thumb|left|A MTT painted with the colors of the Confederacy of Independent Systems]]
During the [[Battle of Ryloth/Legends|Battle of Ryloth]], [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]] used many of these units to ship treasure from across the planet to the capital where the main base was, although two units were destroyed by [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]].<ref name="Liberty on Ryloth">{{TCW|Liberty on Ryloth}}</ref>

They were also utilized at [[Battle of Dathomir|Dathomir]] and [[Battle of Onderon/Legends|Onderon]], where they deployed [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|super battle droids]].

The MTT was seen in combat on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and many other battlefronts (including the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]]). MTTs were still in use as of the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]].<ref name="SW:CW" />

[[File:MTTopenforbusiness-SWE.png|thumb|right|MTT deploying B1 battle droids]]

==Behind the scenes==
Multi-Troop Transports first appeared in [[1999]] with the release of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] and its tie-ins.

The revised rough draft script of Episode I described the MTTs as "Maxi-Troop Transports." George Lucas' original design requests spoke of a massive locomotive-type vessel knocking everything down in its path. With this direction, the Art Department crafted a number of battering ram and literal locomotive designs. In the end, Doug Chiang incorporated animalistic qualities, giving the MTT the characteristics of a massive elephant, with a high "forehead" and gun turret "tusks."<ref name="DB-Trade Federation AAT Armored Assault Tank">{{DB|vehicle|tfed_aat|Trade Federation AAT (Armored Assault Tank)}}</ref>

Although stated to have a maximum altitude of 4 meters in some sources, in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|1999 Star Wars : Episode I The Phantom Menace videogame]]'s level "Gardens of Theed", it can be seen landing from much higher.

In the [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' and its [[2002]] [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns|expansion pack]], MTTs serve as the "assault mech/troop transport" unit for the Trade Federation. Players are provided them in several missions of the campaign, and more may be built at mech factories for 200 units of food and 350 units of [[Nova crystal/Legends|nova crystals]].

MTTs were also re-imagined in LEGO form in [[2005]] for ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]'' and its [[2007]] [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|compilation re-release]].
